📝Russian Footprint📝

Russia helped Iranians carry out and plan strikes against CIA facilities in the Middle East. At least, that's what Reuters claims, citing four sources familiar with U.S. intelligence data.

This concerns attacks in March: in one operation, a Shahed-136 drone struck the U.S. embassy residence building in Saudi Arabia, and in another—a facility in Iraqi Kurdistan. There were other incidents as well, but all of them resulted in no casualties or injuries.

The Iranian UAVs that struck their targets allegedly possessed enhanced accuracy thanks to the installation of navigation modules from the "Kometa" series. Moreover, U.S. officials note that few besides Russia could possess such sensitive intelligence data.

Although all this sounds logical, there is some skepticism. It's unlikely Tehran didn't know about CIA facilities in its own backyard, especially if they were located in American embassies. And talk of "Kometas" in Iranian "Shaheds" has been around for a while, but objective evidence is scarce.

❗️However, such news is a good thing. The U.S. openly participates in organizing AFU attacks on Russian regions, and it's worth responding in kind. On paper, one can deny everything, but in practice help Iranians as needed and as capabilities allow—which, while limited, do exist even in terms of technical intelligence.

And failing to use such a rare opportunity to inflict serious complications on American foreign policy (at a time when the U.S. is fully exploiting Russian problems)—that's something from the realm of medicine.

💬 IRGC to Jordanian, Kuwaiti peoples: US violating your countries’ sovereignty

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) says it is the United States that, through its military bases in Kuwait and Jordan, has violated the two countries’ sovereignty, emphasizing that Iran has the legal right to target aggressors and those responsible for killing its people wherever they launch attacks.

In separate statements addressed to the peoples of Kuwait and Jordan early Wednesday, the IRGC said US military bases in the two countries operate under American control rather than the authority of their host governments, arguing that the presence of such bases constitutes a violation of national sovereignty.
​
The IRGC said its forces had targeted US military positions in Kuwait and Jordan in response to repeated US attacks on Iran.
​
According to the statements, IRGC forces carried out drone strikes on an arms depot, a Patriot air-defense system and an MQ-9 drone hangar at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. They also targeted Camp Udairi, killing and injuring several US forces and causing heavy damage to several helicopters and drones.
​
In Jordan, the IRGC said it had destroyed a US THAAD missile-defense radar, a Patriot system and a C-RAM radar, while also setting fire to fuel tanks, a large helicopter equipment depot and a helicopter maintenance facility.
​
The IRGC referred to Wednesday’s funeral of the remains of 168 people, including schoolchildren, killed in airstrikes in Minab in the opening hours of the recent US-Israeli war, saying crimes against the Iranian people continue, with some of them being committed using bases in Kuwait and Jordan.
​
“It is our legal, religious and logical right to target the aggressor against our country and those who have killed our children wherever they launch their attacks,” it said.
​
The IRGC also emphasized that Iran fully respects the independence and territorial integrity of Jordan and Kuwait.
​
“It is the United States that has violated your territorial integrity and sovereignty, not us. We are targeting the lands occupied by the US army—an army that knows nothing but committing crimes.”

📡 IRGC warns against using alternative routes to Strait of Hormuz after vessel catches fire

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has warned vessels against using alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz, saying the waterway’s entrances and exits are under its “absolute control,” after a vessel caught fire.

In a statement early Wednesday, the IRGC said three vessels had attempted to pass through an unsafe route in the Strait of Hormuz, adding that one of them caught fire while the other two quickly turned back.
​
“The IRGC Navy stresses that the Strait of Hormuz is under our control and will remain completely closed as long as US acts of aggression in the region continue. No oil tanker will be allowed to enter or leave, and any vessel that falls for US deception and attempts to pass through without coordinating with the Islamic Republic of Iran will suffer the same fate,” the statement said.
​
The IRGC also urged the United States to stop “acts of aggression” in the sensitive region and warned against endangering commercial shipping and global energy security.
​
“End these interventions, which will only lead to an energy crisis and a shortage of agricultural fertilizers around the world. These mischiefs will bring you nothing but further discredit and an irreversible defeat that you will soon have to face.”
​
Earlier, the IRGC Navy issued a stern warning to vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, urging them to use only routes designated by Iran.
​
“The entrances and exits of the Strait of Hormuz are clearly defined and under our absolute control,” the IRGC Navy said, adding: “These alternative routes are unsafe and dangerous. We warn against using them, as doing so will have serious and irreversible consequences.”
